_meta.description: Alliance-sourced cheat sheets: troop comps, hero lineups, event timing.
_meta.sourceNote: Comp guides cross-checked against kingshotguide.org, kingshotmastery.com, kingshotwiki.com. SQB should verify against alliance practice.

guides.title: Bear Trap — Rally Lead
guides.summary: Best heroes & troop split when you are leading the rally

blocks.title: Best heroes (Gen 3 lead)
items: Best overall: Amadeus · Petra · Merlin
Low-spender alt: Zoe · Petra · Merlin
F2P fallback: Zoe · Jabel · Quinn
Use attack/rally widgets — not economy heroes (don't use Diana over Quinn)

blocks.text: 5,000 Infantry floor (Gen 4+): At 1/10/89, check absolute troop count — if 1% is under 5,000 infantry, bump infantry % until you're above the floor or damage gets penalized.

blocks.title: Leader checklist
items: Fill rally to your max capacity — leader sets total troop cap.
Bear deals no return damage; prioritize archer-weighted damage over survival.
Coordinate with R4/R5 on how many rallies to run vs how many joiners are online.
Upgrade Bear Trap building — each level adds +5% attack to all troop types in the event.

guides.note: Widgets matter for rally lead. Marlin (attack widget) beats Jaeger on rally lead even though Jaeger has higher raw stats for solo marches.

guides.title: Bear Trap — Joining Rallies
guides.summary: Joiner heroes, troop splits & the 2–3 vs 4–5 rally question

blocks.title: How joiners actually work
blocks.body: Joiners contribute their own troops (which inherit the leader's stats/buffs) plus only the 1st skill of their 1st hero. The game picks the top 4 highest-level joiner skills across the whole rally. Hero slot order beyond #1 does not matter for joiners.

rows: Flat lethality / attack buffs — stack multiplicatively
Amane, Margot, Vivian, Wee & Woo, Ava
Pairs well with Chenko-type; don't stack duplicates blindly
Defensive or economy skills can displace a good damage skill
Valid and often correct — see strategy below

blocks.title: Joiner troop ratio
blocks.body: Send 0% infantry as a joiner. Split capacity 20% cavalry / 80% archers (e.g. 14K cav + 55K arch on a 69K march). Your troops still count toward personal damage score and help the rally.

blocks.title: 2–3 full rallies vs 4–5 thin rallies?
items: Fewer, fuller rallies usually win when coordination allows. Top-4 joiner skill cap means spreading heroes across 5 rallies dilutes buffs.
R4/R5 count online joiners with S-tier heroes before opening rallies.
Run 2–3 rallies with full troops + assigned Chenko/Amadeus/Yeonwoo until top-4 skills are filled.
Once 4 strong joiner skills are locked, extra members send troops only — never a bad hero.
Open a 4th/5th rally only if unused S-tier joiners remain AND troops can fill it.
Hero + no troops? Rarely worth it — sacrifices personal score and rally mass.
Hero + troops in many rallies? Only if each rally gets a unique high-level joiner skill.

blocks.text: Alliance callout in chat: "Rally 1 needs Chenko + Amadeus — who's got Yeonwoo? Everyone else troops-only unless asked."

guides.title: Attack Rallies — Castles & Structures
guides.summary: Hero lineups & formations for taking keeps, turrets & outposts

rows: Attack first — see garrison guide for 2nd rally

blocks.title: Attack joiners
blocks.body: Stack offensive joiner skills like Bear Trap: 2× Chenko + 2× Amane is the damage ceiling; 4× Chenko is easier to coordinate. Joiner troops inherit leader stats — send a full march when you can.

blocks.title: Castle / structure tips
items: Use attack widgets on rally lead — check hero gear before launching.
Scout the garrison comp when possible and counter infantry-heavy setups with more archers.
Double-rally: attack rally lands first; garrison rally ~5 seconds behind (separate guide).
Special buildings (turrets, outposts) use the same attack logic — infantry-heavy defenders mean more archers.

guides.title: Garrison & Defense — PvP
guides.summary: Holding castles, structures & reinforcing allies under attack

rows: ~2.24× Defense Up (two def types on one skill)
When leadership assigns a non-hero reinforcement slot

blocks.title: Garrison joiner mechanics
blocks.body: Garrison strength comes from stacking the same defensive skill type across joiners — not from one superstar lead. Mismatched joiner heroes waste slots. Follow R4/R5 assignments; default to Saul if unsure.

blocks.title: While holding a structure
items: Watch infantry count — if it drops, queue an infantry-heavy reinforcement rally.
Use garrison/defender widgets on lead heroes, not attack widgets.
Voice chat helps for double-rally timing and reinforcement calls.
If attack rally captures first, recall attack heroes before garrison lands so defenders swap in.

guides.note: Reinforcing an ally's city under PvP attack = same garrison joiner logic (Saul/Gordon stack). See Vikings guide for Viking Vengeance — different goal (kills vs survival).

guides.title: Viking Vengeance — Reinforcement
guides.summary: NOT the same as PvP garrison — optimize for kills, not survival

blocks.text: Key difference from PvP garrison: Vikings score on kills, not holding. Use Bear Hunt lethality heroes when reinforcing allies — NOT Howard/Gordon/Saul defensive stacks.

rows: Infantry first, then cavalry — skip archers early
Empty city — let reinforcements get kills

blocks.title: Viking rules of thumb
items: Send infantry/cavalry out to reinforce — troops at home earn almost nothing.
After wave 9 / 19 ends, pull one march back for HQ defense on wave 10 / 20, then return to reinforcing.
Waves 7, 14, 17 hit online players only — prioritize reinforcing active members before those.
Gen 3 Guard Station example: Amadeus · Jabel · Saul (adjust to your roster).

guides.title: Resource Gathering — Heroes & Marches
guides.summary: One Rare hero per resource; 100% single troop type per march

blocks.title: Troop setup
blocks.body: Send 100% of one troop type per march (not a combat split). Use your highest load-tier troops so the node clears in one trip. Match gathering research buffs to the troop type you're sending when possible.

blocks.title: Efficiency tips
items: Target level 6–8 tiles when your march capacity allows — higher yield per trip.
Send enough troops to clear the node in one trip; partial loads waste time.
Inside alliance territory = gathering speed bonus from alliance tech.
Early game: Gordon (+25% speed & +25% march capacity) until blue heroes are leveled.
Planning ratio for stockpiles: roughly 20 bread : 20 wood : 4 stone : 1 iron.

guides.note: During gathering events, match the hero to the resource the event scores — verify the live task list before committing all marches.

guides.title: Troop Formations — Quick Reference
guides.summary: One-page ratio lookup by activity & generation

blocks.text: Format is Infantry / Cavalry / Archers. Save these as march presets before events — don't build comps mid-fight. Counter-scout before deviating from defaults.

blocks.title: Hero pairing hints (Gen 3)
items: Bear lead: 2 archer heroes + 1 rally buff hero at 10/10/80
Attack rally: Amadeus · Petra · Marlin at 50/20/30
Garrison: Eric · Jaeger · Hilde at 60/15/25 + Saul joiner stack
Solo / AC: Amadeus · Petra · Jaeger (widgets don't apply)

guides.title: Formation Presets — What to Save (1–8 Slots)
guides.summary: Priority order for saved march formations on a Gen 3 account

blocks.title: How to read this
blocks.body: Assumes an active Gen 3 alliance member (Bear every 2 days, some PvP, occasional AC/Vikings). Slots = saved troop ratios; swap heroes at send time. Priority = frequency × cost of getting it wrong × how unique the split is.

rows: Chenko · Amadeus · Yeonwoo — or troops only
Bear Trap joins (most members join more than lead)
Attack: Amadeus · Petra · Marlin · Solo/AC: Amadeus · Petra · Jaeger
Attack rallies, castle/turrets/outposts, solo PvP, Alliance Championship
Castle, outposts, flags, PvP ally reinforce
Map gathering — highest load tier, one resource per preset
KvK stall, emergency city defense, SOS reinforce
Viking Vengeance ally reinforce (kills, not hold)

blocks.text: Slot 1 swap: If you lead bears more than you join, make slot 1 Bear lead 10/10/80 and bump joiner to slot 3.

blocks.title: Don't waste slots — these share one preset
items: Attack rally = AC = solo PvP = outpost attack → all 50/20/30
Castle garrison ≈ outpost hold → both 60/15/25
Bear lead, bear join, gather, and Viking reinforce each need their own slot

blocks.title: Role variants
items: Join bears only, never lead: 1 Join → 2 Attack → 3 Garrison (skip bear lead until slot 4+).
R4/R5 bear lead: 1 Lead → 2 Attack → 3 Join.
Gather/farm alt: Move Gathering to slot 2 or 3 if the account rarely fights.
Slot 8 alt: Counter vs cavalry 60/10/30 instead of Viking preset if you scout PvP often and rarely play Vikings.

blocks.text: Gen 4 prep: Replace bear lead with 1/10/89 and verify the 5,000 infantry floor. Joiner stays 0/20/80.

blocks.title: How AC differs from rally PvP
blocks.body: Alliance Championship fights are solo marches — widgets do not apply. Pick heroes on raw stats, not rally widgets. Your buffs are snapshotted at registration (pets, alliance tech, consumables) and locked for the whole event.

rows: Activate pet skills, combat buffs, appointments first
Leadership moves you — register your best once

blocks.title: Lane strategy (alliance coordination)
items: Main lane (~20 fighters): Top power — win outright, max eliminations (2-cap per march).
Second lane (~20 fighters): Also built to win — losing both priority lanes loses the round.
Sacrifice lane: Stall, waste enemy eliminations, preserve buffers. Minimal consumables.
Round 1: spread for intel. Later rounds: reassign based on battle reports.

blocks.text: 50/20/30 is the baseline — R4/R5 may call 6/2/2 or counter-builds after scouting. Don't freelancing a weird split without approval.

guides.title: Swordland Showdown
guides.summary: Roles, building priority & when defense heroes beat attack heroes

blocks.title: Event basics
blocks.body: Bi-weekly 1-hour alliance PvP battlefield. Score Relic Points from buildings, baggage trains, undercellars, and kills. Troops are injured only (no permadeath). Personal rank rewards often matter as much as the alliance win.

rows: Garrison leads — Eric · Jaeger · Hilde, 60/20/20. Howard + Quinn classic duo (−40% damage taken)
Offensive solo marches — hunt enemy troops, burn cities off buildings
Join garrisons, gather scattered points, undercellars, baggage trains

blocks.title: Building capture priority
items: 1. Royal Stables — halves teleport cooldown (capture first)
2. Bell Tower — halves capture time on everything else
3. Sanctums — point engine; hold both if possible
4. Abbeys — fill remaining marches
5. @ 15 min: Hall of Reformation (+15% dmg/def), Merc Camp, Swordshrine opens — Reformation is high value; don't tunnel Swordshrine alone

blocks.text: Voice chat + map labels from R4/R5. If outmatched, farm personal Relic Points rather than throwing everything at unwinnable fights.

guides.title: Outposts, Flags & Territory
guides.summary: Same comp logic as castle — with widget nuance for solo garrison

blocks.title: Same as castle battle?
blocks.body: Mostly yes. Attack rallies on outposts/flags use the same attack heroes and 50/20/30 default as castle/turret fights. Garrison uses Eric · Jaeger · Hilde at 60/15/25 with Saul/Gordon joiner stacks.

rows: Same — defensive widgets activate even solo

blocks.text: Widget note: Defensive widgets activate when garrisoning rallyable locations (outpost, flag, node) — even if you're alone. Use defender-widget heroes here, not attack widgets.

blocks.title: Territory tips
items: Reinforcing an ally's outpost under attack = PvP garrison rules (Saul stack), not Viking rules.
Scout the garrison before attacking — swap to 30/20/50 vs infantry-heavy defenders.
Double-rally still applies: attack to dislodge, garrison rally ~5s behind.

rows: Widgets don't apply — raw stats win
Same as solo; prep preset saves time

blocks.text: Rule of thumb: Rally/garrison = check widgets. Solo = ignore widgets, pick highest stat heroes.

guides.title: Watchtower Intel — KvK & Golden Glaives Timing
guides.summary: Complete vs claim, expiration clocks, and skip-and-burst prep for KvK D1/D3/D5

blocks.text: Two different scoring rules — don't mix them. KvK prep awards 6,000 pts when you finish a mission. Golden Glaives Dim Goldstones award on claim/redemption during the event window. Holding an unclaimed reward helps GG; it does not delay KvK points — those land at completion time.

blocks.title: Refresh schedule & mission board
blocks.body: Intel refreshes 3 times per day at 00:00, 08:00, and 16:00 UTC. Each drop adds a visible batch (wilderness victories, refugee rescues, encampment attacks, plus rebel bounty chains). Rebel bounties are hidden until you clear the visible set — typically up to ~5 bounties per full clear before the board empties.

blocks.text: Expiration is time-based, not a mission-count limit. Each mission expires roughly 15–16 hours after it spawns. There is no hard cap on how many unfinished missions can queue on your map — the clock is what bounds stacking. Example: missions from the 16:00 UTC batch expire around 07:00 UTC the next day. You cannot hoard intel across multiple calendar days; you can only overlap ~1–2 refresh cycles before older missions time out.

blocks.title: Delayed spawn / backlog behavior
blocks.body: If you don't finish missions before the next refresh, they can linger on the map. As you clear the current visible set, older missions from the previous drop may surface — this is the "backlog" players describe. Practical depth is still limited by the 15h expiration timer on each spawn, not by a hidden stack number.

blocks.title: KvK prep intel days (D1, D3, D5) — 6,000 pts per completion
rows: ❌ Don't start or finish any intel
Leaves one full refresh cycle untouched for the burst
KvK points score the moment you finish each mission
Finish the prior day's 16:00 batch before ~07:00 expiry
Extra refresh batch still scores on completion today
Claim timing does not affect KvK prep points

blocks.title: KvK intel day checklist
items: Intel scores on D1, D3, and D5 only — each day gets its own 16:00-skip → 00:00-burst window.
Don't apply GG "hold the claim" logic to KvK unless you also control when you complete.
Completing intel before midnight on an intel day scores that day — completing after 00:00 scores the new UTC day.
Rough ceiling per intel day: ~2 overlapping refresh cycles + rebel chains × 6,000 pts — stamina is usually the real limit.

blocks.title: Golden Glaives — Dim Goldstones score on claim
Advanced GG stacking (optional)
items: Hold two refresh cycles of completed-but-unredeemed missions (~16 hours before GG opens).
When GG goes live, redeem the first batch → delayed spawn can surface a second batch → redeem again within the first 8 hours of the event.
Community guides estimate ~16 extra Dim Goldstones vs playing straight through — bounded by the same expiration clocks.

blocks.text: KvK + Golden Glaives overlap: When both are live, you can complete for KvK points and claim during GG for Dim Goldstones on the same mission — but only if the completion timestamp falls on the KvK intel day and the claim happens while GG scoring is active. Plan the 00:00 UTC burst when both events start together.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Completing intel before midnight on the wrong prep day — points land on completion, not claim.
Skipping intel for multiple days hoping for a mega stack — missions expire in ~15h, not days.
Thinking there's a max mission count — it's the timer that kills old spawns.
Using GG hold-claim advice on non-GG days when you needed KvK completions instead.

guides.note: Sources: kingshotwiki.com Kingdom of Power, kingshotguide.org Golden Glaives stacking guide, community Watchtower behavior. SQB verify against in-game timers for your Watchtower level.

guides.title: Eternity's Reach — Copper & Skill Tree
guides.summary: 30-min safe instance — hunt guards, cycle vein procs, sprint Fracture Veins, snipe Peak in final 7 min

blocks.text: Safe event map. Separate battlefield instance — no troop permadeath, no attacks on your main city. Veins and the center can be contested. If defeated at a mine or in PvP, your hero enters a ~5 minute cooldown (marches can still go out without heroes).

blocks.title: Event basics
blocks.body: Bi-weekly solo competitive event (~30 minutes per match). Goal: accumulate the most copper ore for rank rewards (Governor Charm materials — top 10 finishes matter). You're matched into a lobby (~100 players, similar server age/power band). Register same-day — pick a time slot you can play the full 30 minutes actively (~10–15 min before it opens). Recall all troops before entering the instance.

blocks.title: Before the match
items: Pick a time slot you can babysit — this is not a background event.
Recall troops home first; use teleporter if marches are still marching.
Six march slots help; five well-managed is enough.
Loot wagon is a free extra collector — does not use a march slot. Keep it moving.

blocks.text: Ignore the default advice. Fighting whales for L3 veins and camping the Peak all match is a trap for most players. Efficiency beats raw power — hunt guards, cycle vein bonuses, and sprint Fracture Veins instead of slow passive mining.

blocks.title: Recommended skill path — Right · Right · Left · Left · Right
rows: Core income once hunting loop is online
Faster guard hunts and vein cycling
5,000 copper when occupying a vein (60s CD)
★ Most important — the vein proc engine
Clears Fracture Veins faster during spawn waves
Use on regular veins late — not Fracture Veins

blocks.title: Phase 1 — Early game (first ~10 min): hunt guards
blocks.body: Focus on killing Cesares Guards to earn XP and unlock the skill tree. Target Level 2 guards first — more XP than L1, still manageable F2P. Use the Search / Find button; skip guards already under attack. Loot mine guards heavily — scattered copper piles are a massive boost; send your loot wagon immediately after kills.

blocks.title: Guard hunting tips
items: Prioritize L2 guards until skills are unlocked, then keep hunting all match for 1,500 copper/kill.
Don't stop after max skills — uncontested guards stay on the map.
Defeated guards drop scattered ore — wagon + manual collection adds up fast.
Avoid unnecessary PvP — hero cooldowns slow your loop.

blocks.title: Phase 2 — Mid game: the 60-second vein cycle
blocks.body: Once Tier 3 Left (5,000 copper on vein occupy) is unlocked, add the vein proc loop alongside guard hunting. Every ~60 seconds: occupy a copper vein → trigger the 5,000 bonus → recall → wait for CD → repeat. You're farming the skill proc, not trying to camp and mine. Use L1 guarded veins if contested — the bonus matters more than holding tier.

blocks.text: Vein tap timing: Track the event timer (e.g. :00, :01 each minute). Recall around the 40s mark if needed so you can re-send on cooldown. Failed occupies still often pay if the proc fires — don't rage-fight over a contested tile.

blocks.title: Mid game priorities
items: Keep the 60s vein cycle running on one dedicated march slot.
Use remaining slots for guard hunting between vein sends.
When skills are maxed, gather from L2 veins if available (L3 usually whale territory).
Fall back to L1 veins for steady income — something beats nothing.
Activate T5 gather boost manually on regular veins only — it does not boost Fracture Veins.

blocks.title: Phase 3 — Fracture Vein waves (2 per match)
blocks.body: Two Fracture Vein rounds spawn during the 30 minutes (~4,000 capacity, ~200 copper/sec vs ~16/sec on normal L2). Watch the mini-map countdown. At the 60-second warning, recall all marches so you're ready the instant they spawn — first arrivals win contested tiles. Send every free slot. If you missed a wave by 2+ minutes, skip stale veins and return to guard/vein cycling.

blocks.title: Phase 4 — Final 7 minutes: Peak of Eternity
blocks.body: The Peak of Eternity (center tower) unlocks with 7 minutes left — not at match start. Make one quick capture attempt when it opens; even a brief touch can land you on the occupation leaderboard for a large end-of-match bonus (often 40k–80k pool split by hold time). Don't overcommit — return to Cesares + vein cycling unless you're strong enough to hold.

blocks.title: Four parallel income streams (run all at once)
rows: Kill Cesares for XP early, then 1,500 copper/kill + wagon loot
Recall early, send all marches on spawn
One quick capture attempt, then back to loops

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Camping high-tier veins instead of cycling the 5k proc.
Fighting for the Peak all match — wastes marches early.
Letting the loot wagon sit idle.
Burning T5 active on Fracture Veins (wrong target).
Stopping guard hunts after skills max out.
Hero on cooldown → entire operation stops (send hero-less marches instead).
Joining a time slot you can't actively play for 30 minutes.

guides.note: Sources: SQB alliance practice, kingshotwiki.com, kingshotmastery.com, kingshotguide.org. Skill names vary slightly by patch — verify T3 Left = 5k on vein occupy in-game. Rewards scale hard by rank; top 5 ≫ top 10 ≫ mid pack.

guides.title: Terror Rallies — Safe / Maybe / No Cheat Sheet
guides.summary: What actually wins terror fights — captain stats, troop tier, rally fill, joiner skills

blocks.text: Assumption for this table: Full rally capacity, Gen 3 formation (10/10/80), and a realistic mix of joiners — some Chenko/Amadeus/Yeonwoo in slot 1, plus a few bad heroes (Jabel, Gordon, Howard, Diana) stealing skill slots. Stamina is refunded if the rally fails.

blocks.title: What actually determines win / loss
blocks.body: Terror rallies are leader-driven. Joiner account power and joiner gear do not apply — only the captain's stat sheet buffs everyone. City level (TC) matters only indirectly (unlocks troops, Command Center, heroes).

blocks.title: Factor priority (most → least important)
rows: Attack, Lethality, Health, Defense from research + Governor Gear + Charms + Chief Gear — multiplies every troop in the rally
All 9 expedition skills + exclusive gear apply; Mythic widgets are multiplicative
Highest troop tier in the rally
Sets base stats for the entire army — one T7 joiner drags the whole rally down
Command Center sets rally cap; empty slots = free damage left on the table
Only Hero 1 skill 1 counts; game picks 4 highest levels — Jabel/Gordon/Howard skills are dead weight
Joiners bring troop count + maybe one skill; their research and gear are ignored
Leader march size helps, but CC rally capacity + fill rate matters more for terrors

blocks.title: Gen 3 cheat sheet — should you lead this terror?
rows: CC 10 low fill or weak lead
CC 15–18+, T8, Gen 3 mythic lead, 80%+ fill
CC 12–15 full rally OR CC 18+ with weak joiners
CC 18–22+, T8+, Amadeus/Petra/Marlin lead, 90%+ fill, 2+ Chenko-type joiners
CC 15–18 if top alliance player leads; mixed joiners
Missing T8 or Gov Gear; CC < 15; bad hero lead
CC 22–26+, T9+, top roster + whale fill

blocks.text: Mixed joiner penalty: Each wasted skill slot (Jabel lead, Gordon, Howard, Diana, duplicate low combat skills) effectively drops you one row — L5 "Safe" becomes "Maybe" if 2+ joiner slots are bad. Coordinate in chat: "Need 4× Chenko/Amadeus slot 1 — troops only after that."

blocks.title: Rally capacity quick ref (captain CC → total troops)
Captain checklist (before you open)
items: Are you top ~10–15 alliance power for this content? If not, join — leading wastes 25 stamina and everyone's time.
Tap the rally info panel — confirm captain bonuses and joiner skills before timer expires.
L5+: confirm you have T8 troops + Governor Gear equipped.
Post per-joiner troop cap: (total capacity − your march) ÷ joiners.
Leader heroes: offensive mythics (Gen 3: Amadeus · Petra · Marlin) — not economy/defense heroes.
Formation: 10 / 10 / 80 (Gen 3). Gen 4+: keep ≥5,000 infantry absolute count.

blocks.title: Joiner quick rules
items: Joining costs 0 stamina — default role for most SQB members.
Hero 1: Chenko, Amadeus, or Yeonwoo — or troops only (better than Jabel/Gordon/Howard).
Send highest troop tier you have; L5+ rallies require T8 in your march.
Enable Auto-Join (War → Rally → Auto-Join) for passive Satin farming.
Regimental Expansion research matters — bigger march = bigger contribution.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
items: Leading with Jabel / Gordon / Howard — defensive or economy skills don't scale terror damage.
Opening L5 without T8 or Governor Gear.
Letting joiners lock the rally half-full with weak troops.
Multiple Jabel leads — four bad skills beats two good ones + two bad.
Using TC level as a proxy — CC + captain stats + troop tier are the real checks.
Ignoring the rally panel — highest-level skill wins even if it's a gathering skill.

guides.note: Community-synthesized for Gen 3 / K1762 — not official HP thresholds. When in doubt, join an alliance L3–L4 first and watch the battle report. Sources: kingshotwin.com terrors/rallies guides, kingshotwiki.com. SQB: adjust Safe/Maybe rows as kingdom age advances.
